title: Veripsa Coordination Brief
description: A stable, read-only, versioned, content-free machine-readable form of the same pre-merge coordination judgment Veripsa already renders as a GitHub check + PR comment. It SERIALIZES the existing verdict/relationship output of core.main_impact_surface for ONE acting change (a PR) against a protected branch, tied to an exact acting_head_sha + base_sha. It carries paths, symbol names, line numbers, in-flight PR refs, and a content-free coupling hash ONLY -- never source bodies, diff bodies, secrets, or raw graph-size counts (fan-in, symbol counts, downstream-file counts, thresholds). It is deterministic (same inputs -> same Brief) and consistent with the existing verdict contract (states clear / heads_up / wait_in_line / unknown). Paused is NOT a fifth base state: it is modelled as the ack overlay (ack.state + requires_human_ack on the relevant relationship + action_required).

schema_version.description: The Brief schema major version. Bumped only on a breaking field/enum change; additive fields do not bump it.

kind.description: A stable discriminator so a consumer can recognise a Brief regardless of transport.

repository.description: The repository the acting change targets, promoted to an object so the Brief can pin the code-graph GENERATION the verdict was computed under (a repository-lifecycle / graph-regeneration ordinal). slug is the content-free owner/repo the check already posts to; generation lets a consumer detect a graph regeneration that could invalidate a pinned Brief. generation is null when the caller does not supply one -- a Brief without it is still valid.

slug.description: owner/repo the acting change targets. Content-free (the repo slug the check already posts to).

generation.description: The repository / code-graph generation (a monotonic lifecycle ordinal) the verdict was computed under, when the caller supplies it. A consumer can detect a graph regeneration -- a different generation -- that could invalidate a Brief pinned to the old graph. Null when not supplied. Content-free: an opaque ordinal, NEVER a graph-size count (fan-in, symbol count, downstream-file count).

base_branch.description: The protected branch the acting change is heading to (e.g. main).

acting_change.description: The change this Brief is about, as a content-free ref: PR-<n> (a pull request) or BR-<branch> (a branch reservation with no open PR).

acting_head_sha.description: The exact commit SHA the Brief was computed against (the analyzed head of the acting change). A Brief is ALWAYS pinned to one head; a new head yields a new Brief.

base_sha.description: The exact base-branch tip SHA the analysis was relative to, when the caller supplies it -- the 'base.sha' provenance pin: base_branch names WHICH base and base_sha pins its exact state, so a consumer can detect the base moving under the analysis. Kept flat (rather than nested under a 'base' object) to stay the least-disruptive shape; base_branch + base_sha together carry the base identity. Null when the delivery path did not carry a single base tip (the engine tracks base per-path, not as one branch SHA -- see design doc).

state.description: The base coordination state -- the 1:1 machine form of the check verdict. clear=nothing in flight touches this; heads_up=coordinate (semantic coupling / blast radius / soft overlap); wait_in_line=a direct collision is ahead, land in order; unknown=not enough signal to call this clear. Paused is NOT here (it is the ack overlay).

action_required.description: True iff a merge-gating condition is present: an unresolved conflict marker (a hard build-breaker), OR a material coupling that is un-acknowledged (ack.state in paused/stale_reack). Veripsa is advisory by default; this flag is the ONLY thing that gates a merge, and only when the customer has marked the Veripsa check required in branch protection.

enforcement.description: How Veripsa's signal is enforced. Always 'advisory': Veripsa records and steers; the customer's branch-protection policy decides what blocks. action_required is a SIGNAL that policy may act on, not a Veripsa-imposed block.

redacted.description: True on a pull request from a fork: cross-change refs and base-repo paths are withheld (they would leak the private base repo's in-flight structure to an outside contributor), so relationships carry only the fork's own conflict markers plus the state. Absent/false otherwise.

relationships.description: The coordination relationships between the acting change and the rest of the in-flight world, each a serialization of one signal the check/comment already renders. Deterministically ordered. Empty on a clear PR with no co-signals.

evaluated_against.description: Provenance pins for every OTHER in-flight change the relationships name, each tied to the exact head SHA the analysis saw. This is the field that lets a Brief detect a MOVED partner: if a counterpart's current head no longer equals the head_sha recorded here, the coupling was evaluated against a stale partner and the Brief should be recomputed. The acting change itself is excluded (it is pinned by acting_head_sha). Deterministically ordered by ref. Empty when the Brief names no counterpart change (a clear PR, a fork's redacted Brief, or a first-sync).

evaluated_change.description: One counterpart in-flight change the analysis was evaluated against, pinned to the exact head SHA it had at analysis time. Content-free: a ref, a PR number, a head SHA, and the counterpart's own coordination state -- never a body, a diff, or a breadth count.

ref.description: The counterpart change, as a content-free ref (PR-<n>/BR-<branch>) -- the same ref used in relationships[].related_change / ordered_changes.

number.description: The pull-request number when the ref is a PR (the integer in PR-<n>); null for a BR- branch reservation, which has no PR number.

head_sha.description: The exact head commit SHA the counterpart change had AT THE TIME the analysis ran. A consumer compares this to the counterpart's current head to detect a moved partner. Null only when the counterpart's head could not be resolved (the partner is still listed so it is never silently dropped).

state.description: The counterpart change's own coordination state at analysis time -- the same four base states -- so a consumer sees at a glance whether the partner was itself clear / heads_up / wait_in_line / unknown. Content-free.

relationship_kind.description: Which coordination signal this is -- the enumerated kinds map 1:1 to the engine's relationship capabilities (main_impact_surface + the render layer).

related_change.description: The other in-flight change this relationship is with, as a content-free ref (PR-<n>/BR-<branch>). Null for a structural self-observation with no counterpart change (blast_radius, recurring_contention, co_change, main_moved, the unverified_* / truncated_analysis notes, and landing_order whose ordered set lives in ordered_changes).

evidence_kind.description: What KIND of evidence backs this relationship. structural=a code-graph edge / symbol / line geometry (import, call, shared table, shared config key, shared column, blast radius, dependency DAG); historical=repeated co-change in the repo's landed history; textual=git line geometry (a conflict marker, a likely rebase conflict, a file that moved on the base); unverified=could not be computed or was deliberately suppressed (new path, extractor gap, truncation, hub-dampened coupling).

subject.description: The primary named locus of the relationship: a file path, a symbol name, or null. Content-free (a name Veripsa already surfaces on the comment). The coupling MECHANISM (which edge kind) is deliberately NOT named -- that is the moat.

related_paths.description: Content-free file paths this relationship runs through (e.g. the shared lane, the downstream reach, the moved files). Capped like the comment; NEVER a raw count. Absent when there is no path list.

more_related_paths.description: True when related_paths was capped and more exist -- a qualitative 'and more', never the remaining count (moat).

reach.description: For blast_radius only: a qualitative severity word for how far the change fans out downstream. Never a file count (moat).

basis.description: For recurring_contention only: WHY the file is a chronic contention point, qualitatively. foundation=imported widely; god_file=defines many distinct pieces; both. Never the raw fan-in / symbol count (moat).

ordered_changes.description: For landing_order only: the suggested land order for the contention neighbourhood, most-foundational-first, deduped to one entry per distinct change. In-flight PR refs are customer-facing (the comment numbers them); the code graph's size is not, and is never here.

acting_position.description: For landing_order only: the acting change's 1-based position in ordered_changes, or null if it is not placed.

recommended_action.description: The advisory next step for THIS relationship. land_in_order=wait behind the holder and rebase once; align_before_merge=a foundation you build on is being edited, align to it; coordinate_before_merge=a semantic coupling, revise together; rebase_before_merge=the base or an overlapping insertion point moved, rebase; resolve_conflict_marker=re-resolve an unresolved git marker (build-breaker); free_the_lane=you hold a lane others wait on, land promptly; consider_split=a load-bearing file keeps causing collisions; investigate=an unverified/gap/truncated area to look at; monitor=informational, no required step.

requires_human_ack.description: True iff this specific relationship is part of a MATERIAL coupling that Veripsa pauses on until acknowledged (a direct same-path collision, or a semantic coupling with an in-flight counterpart) AND the acting change is currently material. Exactly mirrors what ack.coupling_snapshot binds to. False on advisory notices, conflict markers (resolve, do not ack), and non-material relationships.

confidence.description: How strong the evidence is. certain=a deterministic fact (an unresolved marker WILL break the build); corroborated=two independent signals agree (a structural edge AND repeated co-change); supported=a single direct structural edge or a surviving collision; likely=a content-free heuristic with no body-level proof ('likely', not 'will' -- rebase-conflict geometry, base-moved overlap, a standalone co-change hint); unverified=could not be computed or was suppressed.

locus.description: The finer point of a collision/conflict when the engine could place one. Content-free: a path, a symbol NAME, and/or line numbers -- never code. All fields optional; the object is omitted entirely when only the file is known and it is already in subject/related_paths.

ack.description: The 一時停止 (pause-and-acknowledge) OVERLAY -- NOT a base state. A material coupling holds the check at action_required until someone records the veripsa-ack label; that flips ack.state to acknowledged. Modelled here as a flag block so the four base states stay exactly four.

label.description: The GitHub label that records an acknowledgement. Adding it is a recorded, conscious stop-and-engage -- NOT an approval, pardon, or sign-off.

required.description: True iff the acting change is in a material coupling that needs acknowledgement (a real in-flight cross-PR collision). False for clear/unknown/advisory-only and on fork PRs.

present.description: Whether the veripsa-ack label is on the acting change right now (caller-supplied from GitHub).

state.description: The overlay state. not_material=nothing to acknowledge; paused=material and un-acked (action_required); acknowledged=label present and bound to the current coupling snapshot; stale_reack=the coupling materially changed since the ack, re-acknowledge; ack_verification_pending=a transient authority read means the ack was neither trusted nor stripped.

coupling_snapshot.description: A stable, content-free 12-hex identity of THIS coupling (the sorted set of partner refs + colliding paths, hashed -- NEVER file contents). An ack binds to it; a materially changed coupling yields a different hash and re-pauses. Empty string when not material.

label_action.description: Informational: 'remove' when a stale ack's label must be taken off so it reads un-acked, else null. The delivery path (not the Brief) performs any label change.

freshness.description: Whether this Brief still describes the state it was computed against. A Brief is pinned to acting_head_sha (+ the counterpart heads in evaluated_against, the graph in graph_source_sha/repository.generation, and the engine tuning in policy_version); the consumer must check status / head_matches before trusting it.

evaluated_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp the analysis was performed, when the caller supplies it. Null when not supplied (kept out of the pure serializer so the Brief stays deterministic -- the delivery path stamps it).

head_matches.description: True when acting_head_sha equals the acting change's CURRENT head at delivery time; false when the head moved under the analysis (the Brief is stale, recompute); null when the caller could not determine it. Retained as the raw signal; `status` is the canonical, explicit freshness verdict derived from it.

analysis_truncated.description: True when the acting change changed more files than Veripsa analyzes in one pass, so the verdict covers only the analyzed subset and an unparsed remainder is unknown-not-clear.

status.description: The explicit, canonical freshness verdict -- the 4-value replacement for the implicit head_matches boolean. current=head still matches; stale=the head moved under the analysis (recompute); unknown=the caller could not determine it; unavailable=freshness could not be established at all (no current-head read happened). When the caller does not supply it, it is derived from head_matches (true->current, false->stale, null->unknown); 'unavailable', which head_matches cannot encode, appears only when supplied. Optional/additive: a Brief without it is still valid.

graph_source_sha.description: The code-graph snapshot / generation SHA the verdict was computed against, when the caller supplies it -- a freshness pin distinct from acting_head_sha (which pins the diff) and repository.generation (a lifecycle ordinal). Lets a consumer detect that the graph the analysis ran on has since changed. Null when not supplied. Content-free.

policy_version.description: The detector / policy revision token the verdict was produced by. DISTINCT from schema_version, which versions the Brief SHAPE, not the engine tuning: two Briefs with the same schema_version may have been produced by different detector revisions, and this token makes that difference detectable. Null when not supplied. Content-free (an opaque revision token).
